title: Manifest toolchain lock
description: Content-addressed provisioning lock for manifest provision. Every tool entry names the artifact kind (binary, python-env, node-env), its per-platform source, a sha256 that a real download/lockfile must satisfy, and an exe_sha256 that is the sole trust anchor toolchain.resolve() verifies against (never the store's own manifest.json) -- see exe_sha256 for its per-kind meaning. An entry with sha256 or exe_sha256: null is unattested and must resolve to BLOCKED, never PASS.

sha256.description: Hash of the downloaded archive/binary, verified by manifest provision before extraction.

exe_sha256.description: The trust anchor `toolchain.resolve()` verifies at every preflight; null is unattested and must resolve to BLOCKED, never PASS, and the store's own manifest.json is never trusted for this value. Meaning depends on `kind` (Correction 3, phase-3-5-decisions.md): for `binary`, the sha256 of the materialized executable's bytes. For `python-env`/`node-env`, the sha256 of the installed DISTRIBUTION SET (every dist-info RECORD, or the node_modules/.package-lock.json packages object) -- never of one console script's bytes, which embed an absolute, store-location-dependent interpreter/launcher path and can never match a committed lock.

console_scripts.description: python-env / node-env only: every console-script relative path (under the materialized env's bin/) a registry check resolves through `store:<bundle>/<relative>`. Not individually hashed -- verified collectively via the bundle's single `exe_sha256` distribution-set digest, plus a per-script existence and launcher-provenance (inside-store) check.

extra_executables.description: binary kind only: an additional subtree extracted from the SAME archive as the primary `bin/<bundle>` executable (no second download) and recorded at `bin/<name>`, independently hashed -- e.g. `node`'s `npm`: `path_in_archive` names the archive-relative subtree directory (`.../lib/node_modules/npm`), `executable_relative` the runnable file inside it (`bin/npm-cli.js`), and `exe_sha256` is that file's OWN hash -- never the primary tool's `exe_sha256`.
